Q300577: City in northern Tamil Nadu on the Palar River.
Its granite Vellore Fort (16th century) saw the 1806 Vellore Mutiny, an early revolt against British rule.
Home of the famous Christian Medical College hospital and VIT university.
The Golden Temple of Sripuram is nearby.
Q204381: Capital of North Kivu in eastern DR Congo, on the north shore of Lake Kivu.
Lies just south of Mount Nyiragongo, whose lava lake erupted into the city in 2002 and 2021.
Twin city of Gisenyi in Rwanda; gateway to Virunga National Park's mountain gorillas.
Captured by M23 rebels in January 2025.
Q209698: City in southern Maharashtra on the Panchganga River.
Called 'Dakshin Kashi' for the Mahalaxmi (Ambabai) temple.
Famous for Kolhapuri sandals, spicy Kolhapuri food and wrestling.
Capital of a Maratha princely state ruled by descendants of Shivaji.
Q2475171: The municipality of Chihuahua, seat of the state capital.
Covers a large area with almost 900 small localities beyond the city.
Q41262: City in the East Midlands of England.
Home of the legend of Robin Hood and the Sheriff of Nottingham; Sherwood Forest is nearby.
Grew with lace-making, bicycles (Raleigh) and tobacco.
Its 'Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem' claims to be England's oldest pub.
Q1891: Capital of Emilia-Romagna in northern Italy.
Home of the University of Bologna (1088), the oldest university in continuous operation.
Famous for its 40 km of porticoes (World Heritage Site) and medieval towers.
Called 'la grassa' (the fat one) for its food: mortadella, tortellini and ragù.
Q3799: Official capital of Benin, on a lagoon near the Nigerian border.
Its name is Portuguese for 'new port'; it began as a slave-trade port.
Capital of French Dahomey from 1900; most government offices are in Cotonou.
Known for its Afro-Brazilian architecture and the Great Mosque in Brazilian church style.
Q200078: Capital of Okayama Prefecture in western Honshu.
Kōraku-en is one of the Three Great Gardens of Japan, next to the black 'Crow Castle'.
Setting of the folktale of Momotarō, the peach boy.
Known for white peaches and Muscat grapes.
Q1861984: City on the mainland part of Penang, Malaysia, across from George Town.
Ceded to the British in 1800 as Province Wellesley.
Includes Butterworth and Bukit Mertajam; linked to Penang Island by two long bridges.
Q17151: Greece's second city, on the Thermaic Gulf in Macedonia.
Founded in 315 BC and named after Alexander the Great's half-sister.
Its Byzantine churches and the White Tower are landmarks; its early Christian monuments are a World Heritage Site.
Birthplace of Atatürk; had a large Sephardic Jewish community for centuries.
Q1006343: City in Thane district north of Mumbai, part of the Mumbai metropolitan region.
Grew rapidly as a commuter suburb on the Western Railway.
Got its first metro line in 2026.
Q167800: City in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq near the Turkish border.
Its Delal Bridge, an old stone bridge, is a landmark.
Close to the Ibrahim Khalil border crossing, Iraq's main gate to Turkey.
Had a famous Jewish community until 1951; known for Newroz celebrations.
Q36796: Twin city with Jamalpur on the Ganges in Bihar.
Mir Qasim, Nawab of Bengal, made it his capital and arsenal in the 1760s.
Jamalpur has one of India's oldest railway workshops (1862).
The Bihar School of Yoga is here; known for gun-making.
Q38811: Capital of Dhi Qar Governorate in southern Iraq, on the Euphrates.
Near the ruins of Ur, the Sumerian city traditionally linked to Abraham, with its great ziggurat.
The Mesopotamian Marshes nearby are a World Heritage Site.
Founded in the 1870s by the Muntafiq tribe.
Q713317: County-level city in Zhejiang under Taizhou.
Its Ming-dynasty city wall, the 'southern Great Wall', was built against pirates.
Has a well-preserved old street (Ziyang Street).
Q515388: City in northern Shaanxi on the Loess Plateau.
Headquarters of the Chinese Communists from 1935 to 1947 after the Long March; called the 'holy land of the revolution'.
Mao and other leaders lived in cave houses (yaodong) here.
The Pagoda Hill is the city's symbol; the Mausoleum of the Yellow Emperor is nearby.
Q337123: City in the Nile Delta on the Damietta branch.
Produces most of Egypt's aluminium cookware.
A historic Sufi centre in the Mamluk era.
Q503056: City in southern Gauteng on the Vaal River, part of the Vaal Triangle.
The Treaty of Vereeniging (1902) ended the Second Boer War.
Sharpeville, site of the 1960 massacre of anti-apartheid protesters, is part of the area.
An industrial centre for steel and coal.
Q868631: Sindh's third city, on the Indus opposite Rohri.
The Sukkur Barrage (1932) feeds one of the world's largest irrigation systems.
The Lansdowne Bridge and the island temple of Sadh Belo are landmarks.
Q570937: Prefecture-level city in Inner Mongolia on the Ordos Plateau.
Holds about a sixth of China's coal reserves and became one of China's richest cities.
Its Kangbashi new town was once called a 'ghost city'.
Home of the Mausoleum of Genghis Khan (a memorial temple).
Q360374: City in southwest Anhui on the Yangtze.
Birthplace of Huangmei opera, one of China's most popular opera styles.
Hometown of Chen Duxiu, a founder of the Chinese Communist Party.
The Zhenfeng Pagoda is the city's landmark.
Q43301: The largest city in California's Central Valley.
Centre of one of the world's richest farming regions (raisins, almonds, grapes).
Its name means 'ash tree' in Spanish.
Gateway to Yosemite, Sequoia and Kings Canyon national parks.
Q184403: Municipality in the São Paulo metro area (the 'ABC region').
Brazil's car-making capital: Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz and others built factories here.
Lula da Silva rose to fame here as a metalworkers' union leader in the 1970s.
Q147975: City in Kaduna State, one of the original seven Hausa city-states (Zazzau).
Home of Ahmadu Bello University, Nigeria's largest university.
Associated with Queen Amina of Zazzau, a 16th-century warrior queen.
Q14168: Capital of West Kalimantan on Borneo, right on the equator.
The Equator Monument marks the line; at the equinox objects cast no shadow.
Founded in 1771 as a Malay sultanate; has a large Chinese (Teochew and Hakka) community.
Lies on the Kapuas, Indonesia's longest river.
Q193021: City on Guanabara Bay north of Rio de Janeiro.
Named after the Duke of Caxias, a 19th-century Brazilian military hero born there.
Has a large oil refinery (REDUC) and chemical industry.
Q200340: City in southern Rajasthan, called the 'City of Lakes'.
Founded in 1559 by Udai Singh II as the capital of Mewar.
The City Palace and the Lake Palace on Lake Pichola are famous; the Lake Palace appeared in the James Bond film 'Octopussy'.
Often called the 'Venice of the East'.
Q44989: Oklahoma's second city, on the Arkansas River.
Once called the 'Oil Capital of the World'; known for Art Deco buildings.
The 1921 Tulsa Race Massacre destroyed the prosperous Black district of Greenwood.
Home of the Bob Dylan Center and the Woody Guthrie Center.
Q185582: City in East Tennessee on the Tennessee River, in the Appalachians.
Home of the University of Tennessee and the 1982 World's Fair Sunsphere.
Gateway to the Great Smoky Mountains National Park.
Q425415: City in southern Sichuan, named after the kapok tree ('panzhihua').
Built from scratch in 1965 as a Third Front steel city in the mountains.
Sits on huge vanadium–titanium magnetite deposits.
Q207324: Odisha's second city and former capital, between the Mahanadi and Kathajodi rivers.
Over 1,000 years old ('Millennium City'); grew around the Barabati Fort.
Famous for silver filigree work (tarakasi) and its Durga Puja.
Seat of the Odisha High Court; birthplace of Subhas Chandra Bose.
Q1187144: County-level city in southwestern Henan under Nanyang.
The city where Fan Zhongyan wrote his famous 'Memorial to Yueyang Tower'.
Q487656: City at the eastern end of the Fergana Valley in Uzbekistan.
Birthplace of Babur, founder of the Mughal Empire.
Over 2,500 years old and a Silk Road city.
The 2005 Andijan massacre of protesters drew world attention.
Q423831: Capital of Ondo State in southwestern Nigeria.
Seat of the Deji of Akure, a Yoruba king.
Home of the Federal University of Technology Akure.
Known for its cocoa farming region.
Q194531: City in southwestern Hunan, formerly Baoqing.
Hometown of Wei Yuan, the Qing scholar who urged China to 'learn from the West'.
Known for the Langshan Danxia landscape and Nanshan grasslands.
Q173121: Capital of the state of Querétaro in Mexico's Bajío region.
Its colonial centre and long stone aqueduct are a World Heritage Site.
The 1917 Mexican Constitution was written here; Emperor Maximilian was executed nearby in 1867.
Today a booming aerospace and manufacturing hub.
Q31487: Poland's second city and royal capital until 1596, on the Vistula.
Its Old Town and Wawel Castle were among the first World Heritage Sites (1978); the Main Square is one of Europe's largest.
Copernicus studied at the Jagiellonian University (1364).
Nearby are the Wieliczka salt mine and the Auschwitz-Birkenau memorial.
Q270176: City in northern Karnataka near Maharashtra and Goa; officially Belagavi.
Karnataka built a second legislature building, the Suvarna Vidhana Soudha, here.
Has a large army cantonment and is famous for 'kunda' milk sweets.
Long disputed between Marathi and Kannada speakers.
Q142811: Pennsylvania's third city, in the Lehigh Valley.
The Liberty Bell was hidden here in 1777 to save it from the British.
With Bethlehem, home of Bethlehem Steel and the 'Christmas City', and Easton, it forms the Lehigh Valley urban area.
Q125293: Puebla, capital of the Mexican state of the same name, was founded by the Spanish in 1531 between Mexico City and Veracruz.
Its historic centre with colourful Talavera-tiled buildings is a World Heritage Site.
Origin of mole poblano sauce and chiles en nogada.
The Battle of Puebla (5 May 1862) against the French is the origin of Cinco de Mayo; the Great Pyramid of Cholula is nearby.
Q7578: Jambi is the capital of Jambi province on the Batang Hari River in Sumatra.
Near the Muaro Jambi temple complex, one of the largest ancient Buddhist sites in Southeast Asia.
Was part of the Malayu and Srivijaya kingdoms; today a centre of rubber and palm oil.
